mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts by more than 5% within two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased construction activity.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST increases by more than 5% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production by more than 2% over three months signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face reduced output and potential earnings declines.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances when INDPRO declines by more than 2% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 in a month signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals increased consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances when RSAFS increases by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure in a high-interest-rate environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the same period, it signals a strong economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase > 2% quarter-over-quarter and UNRATE decrease > 0.3%
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when GDPC1 increases by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3%.
